inputs.text:
Folks, we need to look at what's really going on here. Look at these communities taking to the streets at the "No Kings" rally, fighting back against systemic inequality and authoritarian overreach. How does the ruling class respond? With heavily militarized policing and brute force, protecting entrenched power structures and trying to crush grassroots resistance, labor solidarity, and anti-discrimination movements. 

The establishment throws around words like "lawlessness," but we know whose laws they're really protecting—laws built to preserve hierarchy, marginalize vulnerable groups, and suppress dissent. We already know the brutal reality of this state violence: they confirmed at least 13 arrests in Portland, Denver and... using tear gas against citizens who are simply demanding basic rights and accountability. 

This isn't about public order; it's about shielding the ruling class from accountability. When marginalized communities and activists demand systemic change, the system answers with tear gas and arrests. We have to look at the structural causes behind this unrest: decades of economic exploitation, institutional oppression, and the deliberate erosion of working-class power. You can't police away inequality. True peace will only come when we dismantle these unjust structures, not when we cheer on the officers standing guard over a broken system.
